newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-RYDER CUP ISSUES TO THE FORE IN MALMO.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RYDER CUP ISSUES TO THE FORE IN MALMO.

text.p: Swede Jesper Parnevik and Ireland's Darren Clarke bid to put their British Open disappointment behind them when they play in the Scandinavian Masters which begins on Thursday.

After each holding healthy leads at different stages at Troon they eventually had to settle for joint second behind American Justin Leonard. They can start thinking about revenge of sorts via September's Ryder Cup.

U.S.-based Parnevik, who does not normally play on the European Tour, has another chance to show he is worth a wild card selection for the Valderrama clash, but team captain Severiano Ballesteros will watch only on television after withdrawing from the Malmo field.
Parnevik's inclusion may depend on the form of Ballesteros's Spanish compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal, who currently holds the 10th and last automatic selection place in Europe's Ryder Cup table.
Ballesteros has only two wild cards and could use them on Parnevik and U.S.-based Englishman Nick Faldo if Olazabal clinches an automatic place after the remaining five counting events.
Faldo is 20th in the Ryder rankings with only one more chance to elevate himself into an automatic slot by success in the final major, the U.S. PGA Championship in two weeks' time.

With Olazabal playing in Malmo, where there is a first prize of 125,000 pounds ($203,000) -- and the equivalent in Ryder Cup points -- and total prize money of 750,000 pounds ($1.2 million), a number of Ryder Cup issues could become clearer.

Irishman Padraig Harrington, currently 11th in the Cup table, is in the Scandinavian Masters line-up, as are other players looking to either consolidate or better their placings, including Sweden's Per-Ulrik Johannson (sixth) and ninth-placed Costantino Rocca of Italy. Absent are Thomas Bjorn (seventh) and Miguel Martin (eighth).
European captain Ballesteros pulled out last week citing "the poor state of my game at present".
Defending champion Lee Westwood of England, fourth in the Ryder standings, and Colin Montgomerie, Clarke amd Ian Woosnam -- the top three -- also feature in Sweden.
